title: New Placements and Military Service Hold Extensions — Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
**Placements desk Q&A.** Under Hardship and Protective Holds, the new-placement allowance of a service extension of a Military Service Hold depends on the servicemember's accounts placed with Ridgeline less than two whole months before today, as shown by the placement entries in the servicemember's Placed Consumer Accounts money history. Whole months are the difference in calendar months between the placement date and today, less one when today's day of the month is smaller than the date's day of the month. The allowance keeps the running protection from lapsing while a newly placed account's own request is still being documented, and is added once to the days the service extension adds.

| Accounts placed in that period | New-placement allowance |
|---|---|
| At least the many-placements count of 2 | 30 calendar days (many-placement days) |
| Exactly 1 | 15 calendar days (one-placement days) |
| None | Nothing |

**Which accounts count?** All of the servicemember's accounts placed in the period, not only the held account.

**Two placements in the period?** At least 2: 30 days.

**One placement?** 15 days.

**Example (hypothetical).** Today is 10 May. One account was placed on 11 March and another on 2 May. For 11 March the calendar months are 2, and 10 is smaller than 11, so the whole months are 1: it counts, as does 2 May. Two placements: 30 calendar days are added.
